author: ValWood
body: * **InterPro ID / label** https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro/entry/InterPro/IPR039786/ [protein localization to plasma membrane (GO:0072659)](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/QuickGO/GTerm?id=GO:0072659) * **Example sequences with problematic annotation (ID + gene/protein name):** pombe erf1 https://dev.pombase.org/gene/SPAC1834.01 https://pombase.org/gene/SPAC1834.01 * **Description of issue** Although not technically incorrect, this "localization" term will be phased out for use with single-step procedures where adaptors 'recruit' (see the correct annotation above). So I wondered if this could be removed. Eventually, we will block these types of localization terms in BP except for multistep pathways.
title: InterPro2GO issue: IPR039786/

author: sarach06
body:
Dear Val,
Thank you very much. Yes, makes sense, I removed the term from this entry. This will be visible in InterPro 109.0.

Best wishes,
Sara
